## Argentina, Chile and Peru: combining capital cities with ancient Andean towns

[Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) are too far apart to treat this as a simple road trip. The journey crosses distinct regions of the continent: historic neighbourhoods and tango in Argentina, Chile's Pacific coast and mountain views, and Inca archaeological sites in Peru. A practical itinerary relies on a carefully arranged sequence of flights and several full days for sightseeing.

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Argentina, Chile and Peru as main countries. **Every currently available itinerary in this selection includes additional main countries.** One route visits four countries, including [Brazil](/brazil/), while others also travel through [Bolivia](/bolivia/). The combination's name therefore does not mean there is an existing package limited to these three countries. A journey without Brazil and Bolivia would need to be discussed as a separate adaptation of both itinerary and logistics.

Another major distinction is the Bolivian high-altitude stage. If you travel directly from Santiago to Peru's Sacred Valley, the main challenges are flights and a rapid ascent to higher elevations. On a five-country tour, Atacama, the Uyuni Salt Flat and Lake Titicaca lie between those stages, adding much more lengthy overland travel.

## Existing itineraries: 15 days or 18 days

Comparing three actual offers is more useful than comparing abstract country counts.

- [Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru in 15 Days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) begins in Rio, covers both sides of Iguazu Falls, then [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) and [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), and ends in Peru with the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu, Cusco and Lima. Bolivia and a multi-day Altiplano journey are not part of this itinerary.
- [Five Latin American Countries in 18 Days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) adds Chile's Atacama, [Uyuni](/bolivia/place/uyuni/), La Paz and Titicaca. It is a group itinerary where an off-road high-altitude section follows the city sightseeing.
- [Five Latin American Countries with the Carnival Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) is also an 18-day journey through the same general set of countries, but its opening days are tied to the Champions' Parade in Rio. The event fixes the tour date, so the season for later stages cannot be selected independently.

| Tour | Main difference |
|---|---|
| Four countries, 15 days | Iguazu, capital cities, Machu Picchu |
| Five countries, 18 days | Atacama and Uyuni added |
| Five countries and Carnival | Scheduled around the parade |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki_i_parad_chempionov_karnavala}}

Check the number of overnight stays at key stops, group format, included transfers and actual sequence of airports. Extensive overland travel cannot be assessed from the total duration alone: two 18-day programmes may allocate their days very differently between countries.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires and the Iguazu visit

On the available routes, the Argentina stage follows the [Iguazu Falls](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Travellers see the cascades from the [Brazilian side](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) and then from Argentina. The two national parks are on opposite sides of an international border; passports and entry conditions matter even when the visit is presented as one excursion.

After Iguazu comes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), offering a completely different experience: wide boulevards, San Telmo and La Boca, historic squares, tango, restaurants and waterfronts. The 15-day programme includes sightseeing in the capital and free time. For independent walks, check the hours left after transfers and flights.

The route then continues from Buenos Aires to Santiago. This makes a coordinated flight itinerary particularly important: with separately ticketed connections, passengers may need to collect their luggage and check in again. Connection times should be assessed against airline and airport rules, not just the flight duration.

**Patagonia is not automatically included in every journey through Argentina and Chile.** On the itineraries discussed here, the Argentine stage centres on Iguazu and Buenos Aires. Glaciers and trekking require a different route and additional days. The [Argentina + Chile selection](/multi-country/argentina_chile/) includes separate options that visit Patagonia.

## Chile: why Santiago and Atacama change the journey's duration

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), you can discover colonial buildings, modern neighbourhoods and views of the Andes. The 15-day tour in this catalogue also visits coastal Viña del Mar and Valparaíso. That is a confirmed element of a specific itinerary, not a mandatory feature of every tour that includes Chile.

On 18-day routes, the next stage heads north to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Desert landscapes, sharp differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures and the transition into high-altitude Bolivia require different clothing and logistics. Drives across the plateau can take up much of a day; crossing the Chile–Bolivia border should not be treated as a quick pause between two cities.

Chile conducts separate agricultural inspections on entry. Its SAG authority requires travellers to declare plant and animal products they are carrying. Fresh fruit, meat products, seeds and some souvenirs are subject to the relevant rules. A passport stamp alone does not replace an agricultural declaration.

With limited time, choose between Santiago and the Pacific coast on the four-country itinerary and a different route through Atacama and Bolivia. The distinction is not simply extra kilometres: the latter includes additional high-altitude nights and an expedition stage.

## Peru: making time for Cusco and Machu Picchu

These journeys through Peru include the [Sacred Valley of the Incas](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/), [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). They deserve dedicated, full days; otherwise Peru risks becoming a succession of airports.

Cusco is about 3,350 metres above sea level. After spending time in lowland cities and flying in, travellers may experience headaches and fatigue even without strenuous activity. The order of overnight stays, opportunities to rest after arrival and avoiding demanding exertion immediately after a rapid ascent are therefore important. When travelling through Bolivia, the high-altitude stage begins earlier, but the overall time at elevation becomes longer.

Visiting Machu Picchu requires advance booking through the official system. Tickets specify the date, circuit and entry time. Having “Machu Picchu” in an itinerary does not by itself determine which viewpoints will be accessible: the circuits differ. Rail and onward transfers must match the confirmed admission ticket.

On the five-country tour, the Peru section starts via [Puno and Lake Titicaca](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/). This differs from flying directly into Cusco from Chile. Compare both options for road time, altitude and the number of days remaining for Inca heritage sites.

## When to go: the Andean season and weather in the capitals

**December through March brings summer weather to Buenos Aires and Santiago, but it is the wetter season in the Peruvian Andes.** Warm conditions in the cities do not mean dry trails around Cusco. Rain and clouds can affect experiences at natural sites, and current road-condition reports are essential for high-altitude drives.

The drier season around Cusco is generally May through September. Santiago is cooler during those months, while Buenos Aires experiences Southern Hemisphere winter. No single month provides the very best climatic conditions at every stop on a long journey.

| Region | What to compare |
|---|---|
| Buenos Aires | Heat versus cooler weather |
| Santiago | Summer versus winter rain |
| Cusco | Dry season versus rain |
| Uyuni, if included | Road access and nighttime cold |

The 18-day itineraries add [Uyuni in Bolivia](/bolivia/place/uyuni/) and the high-altitude lagoons. During wet months, standing water can produce a mirror effect on the salt flat, but access to certain sections can change. Dry weather often makes off-road travel easier, although plateau nights can be extremely cold.

Pack layered clothing, a waterproof jacket, warm items for higher elevations, comfortable shoes and sun protection. When flying frequently, baggage allowances for each leg matter, especially if tickets use different fare types.

## Passports, visas, insurance and currencies

Argentina, Chile and Peru have separate entry rules. Check them against each traveller's nationality and actual dates, plus any requirements for countries of transit. Peru's immigration authority advises a passport validity period of at least six months; visa requirements vary by nationality. Argentina and Chile have their own visa systems too. One country's conditions cannot be assumed to apply to the others.

As the existing tours in this selection include Brazil, its entry requirements must also be checked. Bolivia is added on five-country journeys. When visiting both sides of Iguazu, account for the real Brazil–Argentina border crossing even if the overnight stay is in the same city.

Argentina and Chile use different currencies, although both are called pesos. In Peru, expenses are paid in soles. Additional countries require Brazilian reais and Bolivian bolivianos. For international flights and excursions, establish in advance which charges are included and which are paid locally. Cards issued by Russian banks through international payment networks should not automatically be assumed to work abroad.

Choose insurance that covers every country actually visited and takes account of altitude and activities. If the route includes Bolivia and Atacama, ordinary cover designed for city sightseeing may be insufficient. Medical limitations and acclimatisation rates vary by person; a doctor's advice before a demanding high-altitude itinerary is appropriate.

## Choosing a route without unnecessary flights

If Buenos Aires, Santiago and Peru's heritage sites interest you most, start with the [15-day tour through four countries](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/). It provides an existing transport sequence without the Bolivian Altiplano. To add high-altitude lagoons and Uyuni, consider the [18-day programme through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/). For the Champions' Parade, there is a [special Carnival itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/).

For other combinations, visit the [main multi-country travel section](/multi-country/). If your main goal is the high-altitude corridor from Titicaca to Atacama, see [Bolivia + Chile + Peru](/multi-country/bolivia_chile_peru/) for guidance.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a tour covering only Argentina, Chile and Peru?

All currently available itineraries in this selection also include Brazil, and some include Bolivia. A trip limited to exactly three countries can be discussed individually, but it would require revising the flight sequence, duration and services.

### Can I see Buenos Aires, Santiago and Machu Picchu in two weeks?

Such a combination is possible with flights. Ada Tours' 15-day, four-country programme includes all three places together with Brazil and Iguazu. The actual overnight stays are a better measure of comfort than total duration alone.

### Must Machu Picchu tickets be booked in advance?

Yes. Start by choosing a date, an available sightseeing circuit and an entry time through the official ticket platform. Trains and overnight stays around Cusco can then be coordinated.

### What makes adding Bolivia more difficult?

Higher altitude, off-road drives, another international border and cold nights on the Altiplano. The journey becomes considerably more expedition-oriented than a route through major cities and Machu Picchu.

## Argentina, Chile and Peru: where the real adventure lies

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. These are mainly **extended journeys through five to eight countries**, rather than a standalone itinerary visiting only Argentina, Chile and Peru in sequence. From Buenos Aires, the tours head to Chile and then cross Bolivia's highlands before reaching Peru. Some start in Brazil and may also visit Uruguay, Ecuador or Colombia.

The key question for this combination is how much time and energy to devote to **Atacama and the Altiplano**, while preserving enough days for Peru's historic sites. A hike in Patagonia or a multi-day Inca Trail trek should not automatically be expected: not every programme matching this filter includes those separate activities.

## Argentina: waterfalls before the city stage

On the journeys considered here, the Argentina portion generally starts at [Puerto Iguazú](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/). Walkways and paths around the falls bring visitors closer to the cascades than the panoramic viewpoints on the Brazilian side. Allow for the border transfer from Brazil and a possible flight on the same day.

Next comes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Sightseeing, La Boca, San Telmo and a tango show belong to the cultural city programme. This stage provides a change of pace after Iguazu and before the next flight; there is no reason to seek extreme physical activity during a day in the capital.

For example, the [18-day tour through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) visits both sides of Iguazu before Buenos Aires and Santiago. Southern Argentine Patagonia is not on its main route. If glaciers and Patagonia trekking are the priority, compare **other** itineraries rather than assuming they are included here.

## Chile: Santiago, Atacama Desert and altitude

After [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the route heads north to [San Pedro de Atacama](/chile/place/san-pedro-de-atacama/). Desert landscapes replace urban sightseeing. On the existing longer journeys, the stop prepares travellers for crossing into Bolivia and driving off-road through the highlands.

On an Atacama itinerary, the crucial distinction is **between sleeping in the settlement and taking excursions to much higher ground**. Early starts, dry air, sunshine, sharp temperature swings and rough roads call for warm layers, sun protection and a realistic pace. The programme should allow time to adjust. Travellers with medical limitations should discuss plans for the high-altitude stage before booking.

Our [adventure tours in Chile](/interests/adventure/tours/chile/) help distinguish a transit stop in Santiago from an itinerary focused on the desert or mountain trails themselves.

## Why Bolivia lies between Chile and Peru

On the [18-day journey through five countries](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/), the section after San Pedro de Atacama includes an off-road border crossing, Laguna Verde, the geyser area, [Laguna Colorada](/bolivia/place/laguna-colorada/) and the [Uyuni Salt Flat](/bolivia/place/uyuni/). The route then continues via La Paz and Tiwanaku to Lake Titicaca and the Peruvian portion.

These days are **not a decorative interlude** between the countries in the catalogue heading. They are a substantial high-altitude expedition. Unpaved roads and long drives differ sharply from sightseeing in Buenos Aires and Santiago. Compare driving time, number of stops, overnight arrangements and possible changes in weather, and decide whether this section suits everyone travelling.

The same corridor is included on the [20-day, six-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/), while the [32-day journey through eight countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) continues much farther north. These are trips for travellers who want an extensive continental route, not merely a Chile–Peru combination.

## Peru: Lake Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu

After Bolivia, the programme travels through the [Puno and Lake Titicaca area](/peru/place/puno-and-lake-titicaca/) to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/). Some tours include historic stops and visits to Andean settlements along the way. Altitude remains relevant even when a day mainly consists of bus travel and sightseeing.

Travellers usually reach [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) on these tours by train and then an arranged transfer. Walking through the archaeological complex requires suitable shoes and attention to the terrain, but it is not the same product as a multi-day Inca Trail mountain trek. Admission tickets and visitor circuits are regulated separately; the precise circuit needs to be confirmed when booking.

## Comparing the available programmes

| Route | Distinguishing feature |
|---|---|
| [Five countries in 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Atacama, Uyuni, Cusco |
| [Five countries in 19 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-carnival-private-tour/) | Rio celebration plus Altiplano |
| [Six countries in 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Uruguay added |
| [Eight countries in 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Extension into Ecuador and Colombia |

The [five-country New Year journey](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) and [Rio Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) follow much of the same geographical corridor but are tied to particular events and dates. They are best chosen when that celebration is genuinely a priority.

We help compare high-altitude nights, domestic flights, country order and the actual activities on each day. The [Argentina – Chile – Peru selection](/multi-country/argentina_chile_peru/) offers the same geography without a specific theme, while [adventure travel](/interests/adventure/) covers other types of activity.

## Frequently asked questions about adventure travel in Argentina, Chile and Peru

### Can we travel directly from Chile to Peru on these tours?

On the longer journeys described, the itinerary includes **a Bolivian section** with lagoons and Uyuni. Removing it would change the route, transport and duration.

### Is trekking to Machu Picchu included?

A standard Machu Picchu excursion does not mean hiking the Inca Trail. Check the actual means of reaching and visiting the site; a multi-day trek requires a separate description and permits.

### Does acclimatisation matter if most of the programme is sightseeing?

Yes. The elevations of Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons and the Cusco region matter regardless of the physical difficulty of the activities. The pace of ascent and individual medical limitations should be discussed before finalising the journey.

### Will we see Patagonia's glaciers on every tour in this selection?

No. Visiting Argentina and Chile does not necessarily mean visiting Patagonia. Check the days and exact regions in your chosen programme.

## How culture and history unfold in Argentina, Chile and Peru

Our catalogue features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with all three countries on the main itinerary and culture as a substantial focus. **These are real multi-country journeys, not a promise of a separate tour limited to exactly three countries.** Some qualifying programmes also visit Brazil and Bolivia; longer ones may continue to Uruguay, Ecuador and Colombia.

Each of the three countries has a different cultural focus. In [Argentina](/argentina/), it is [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/): neighbourhoods, tango and architecture. In [Chile](/chile/), it is historic [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), with Valparaíso also included on one itinerary. In [Peru](/peru/), the main archaeological experiences are concentrated in [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), the [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/).

The question to ask is: **on which days do travellers actually explore cultural sites, and which days are devoted to nature views or flights?** Iguazu Falls and high-altitude lagoons, for example, are wonderful natural stops, but they should not be counted as museum visits or archaeological excursions.

## Argentina: Buenos Aires and living urban culture

Most qualifying itineraries include sightseeing in Buenos Aires. In [La Boca](/argentina/place/la-boca/), colourful façades and the history of the port district stand out; [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/) is known for older buildings and city life, while [Plaza de Mayo](/argentina/place/plaza-de-mayo/) is at the capital's historic centre. The exact attractions and duration of the walk depend on the individual tour.

Tango has a special place here. Travellers can experience a tango show, often in the evening with dinner. But a tango performance, a dance lesson, a museum and a walk through the neighbourhoods are different experiences. **Mentioning tango in a description of the city does not confirm that an evening performance is included.** Compare the itinerary and services carefully, especially if the tour has only one night in Buenos Aires.

For a journey focused on the country's history, see our [cultural tours in Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/). On an extended multi-country trip, the city section usually takes a few days; balance guided visits and free time.

## Chile: Santiago, the Pacific coast and the limits of time

Chile's cultural section generally begins in Santiago. Itineraries feature the historic centre, Plaza de Armas, La Moneda Palace and the Santa Lucía Hill area. This offers a different historical perspective from Buenos Aires: urban planning beside the Andes, Chilean institutions and civic architecture.

The [15-day tour through Brazil, Argentina, Chile and Peru](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) includes a separate day visiting [Valparaíso and Viña del Mar](/chile/place/valparaiso-vina-del-mar/) after Santiago. It introduces the Pacific coast, urban hills and Valparaíso's historic buildings. For a culturally minded traveller, such a day offers more substance than a simple overnight stop before flying to Peru.

On longer five-country journeys, the Chile section often includes Atacama. The desert and lagoons have their own attractions, but **visiting a natural site is not a substitute for a historical excursion**. If museums, architecture and traditions are priorities, compare the number of city days with the time required to fly to Calama and continue into the highlands.

More options appear in our [cultural journeys through Chile](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/chile/).

## Peru: the Sacred Valley, Cusco and Machu Picchu

In Peru, the itinerary approaches landmarks of the Inca civilisation. The [Sacred Valley](/peru/place/sacred-valley-of-the-incas/) and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) reveal the archaeological side, while [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/) combines Inca heritage with a colonial urban setting.

On the [15-day four-country itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/), the journey from Santiago goes to the Cusco and Sacred Valley region. A separate day covers the valley, including Pisac and Moray; the next is devoted to Machu Picchu and the return towards Cusco. These are specific archaeological stops, not a cursory visit to a Peruvian airport.

The [18-day five-country tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) adds a route through Bolivia and Lake Titicaca before the Peruvian sites. Some itineraries in this group also visit Tiwanaku during the Bolivian section. It is part of Andean history but is geographically **in Bolivia**, so it should not be listed as a Peruvian attraction.

**Machu Picchu requires the correct ticket for the chosen day, entry time and circuit within the site.** Peru's Ministry of Culture operates an official system with distinct visitor circuits and scheduled entry times. Once a programme is chosen, we help coordinate the ticket with travel from the Sacred Valley or Cusco; the actual circuit through the ruins needs separate confirmation.

For a more detailed choice, explore [cultural and historical tours in Peru](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/peru/).

## Which journeys offer more cultural experiences?

| Itinerary | Distinctive focus |
|---|---|
| [Four countries, 15 days](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) | Valparaíso, the Sacred Valley, Machu Picchu |
| [Five countries, 18 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-group-tour-18-days/) | Bolivia and Titicaca added |
| [Five countries with the Champions' Parade](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-rio-champions-parade-18-days/) | Rio festival plus the Andes |
| [Six countries, 20 days](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/) | Uruguay added |
| [Eight countries, 32 days](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) | Ecuador and Colombia added |

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_braziliya_argentina_chili_peru_ru,tour_source_5_stran_latinskoj_ameriki,tour_latin_america_six_countries_20_days_2026,tour_south_america_eight_countries_32_days_2026}}

**The shortest tour is not necessarily superficial, and the longest does not necessarily allow more time in Peru.** A 32-day journey adds countries, airports and excursions. Choose based on actual cultural days at places that matter to you and how transfers between them are arranged.

If your main interests are Buenos Aires, Santiago and Inca sites, compare the [general Argentina – Chile – Peru combination](/multi-country/argentina_chile_peru/) with [multi-country cultural tours](/multi-country/interests/culture-and-history/). The latter includes other geographical combinations and helps you avoid focusing too narrowly on one set of countries.

## Planning: archaeology, flights and altitude

Long flights can separate cultural stops in the southern part of the continent. Buenos Aires and Santiago are at relatively low elevations, while Cusco stands high in the Andes. Travellers who first cross Atacama and Bolivia's Altiplano encounter high-altitude conditions earlier; those arriving in Cusco directly from Chile face a different sequence.

When planning, check:

- **Overnight stays and acclimatisation.** Avoid scheduling the longest, most difficult walking day immediately after a rapid ascent. Discuss specific medical limitations with a doctor beforehand.
- **Tickets and timed entry.** For Machu Picchu, agree on the date, exact visitor circuit and entry time. Not every ticket allows access to every part of the site.
- **Transport.** Account for international connections, transfers to rail or road travel in Peru, and any Bolivia border crossings before finalising the route.
- **Priority sites.** If Inca history is a central interest, allow more time in Cusco or the Sacred Valley rather than adding another city simply to increase the country count.

Countries have separate entry, passport-validity and transit requirements. Check them against nationality and actual connections before buying tickets. Archaeological parks may also restrict access to some areas or hours, so the final plan should follow the chosen official admission tickets.

We help coordinate the excursion calendar with flights, plan a sensible sequence and leave time to acclimatise. Optional private excursions, guide languages and ticket costs depend on the specific offer; terms from one tour should not be carried over to another.

## Frequently asked questions about cultural tours in Argentina, Chile and Peru

### Are there itineraries visiting only these three countries?

The current selection includes journeys with all three on the route, but many also visit Brazil, Bolivia and other countries. Each tour page lists its full itinerary and number of days.

### Which is more important for a history-focused journey: Santiago or Valparaíso?

They offer different experiences. Santiago introduces Chile's political and urban centre; Valparaíso offers a port city with architecture spread across its hills. If time is limited, check whether your itinerary includes a separate coastal excursion.

### Can Machu Picchu be visited without going to the Sacred Valley?

Other options exist, but the [15-day itinerary discussed here](/multi-country/tour/brazil-argentina-chile-peru-15-days/) includes the valley in the sequence. The depth of the visit depends on the ticket, schedule and transport.

### Is Tiwanaku part of the Peruvian stage?

No. Tiwanaku is an archaeological complex in Bolivia. On multi-country journeys, it falls within the Bolivian stage before Titicaca and Peru.

### Does Machu Picchu have to be booked in advance?

Yes. Check official ticket sales and available entry slots for the chosen date and circuit. It is best to coordinate admission before finalising trains, transfers and accommodation.

## Argentina, Chile and Peru on a festive itinerary: where the event takes place

**On our existing event-themed itineraries combining [Argentina](/argentina/), [Chile](/chile/) and [Peru](/peru/), the central celebration is held in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/).** It is either Carnival and the samba-school parade or New Year's Eve on Copacabana. Argentina, Chile and Peru offer other experiences: Buenos Aires and tango, cities and the Atacama Desert, Lake Titicaca and Inca heritage.

## What Argentina, Chile and Peru add after the celebration

### Argentina: Iguazu and Buenos Aires

After Rio, the routes head to Iguazu Falls. The [Argentine side](/argentina/place/puerto-iguazu/) has a different network of paths and viewpoints from the Brazilian side. Next comes [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), where historic districts and a planned tango show provide a cultural continuation. The tango show is a separate part of the itinerary, **not another Carnival celebration**.

### Chile: Santiago and the road to Atacama

The Chilean stage centres on [Santiago](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/) and a flight to Calama, from where travellers continue to San Pedro de Atacama. This brings a marked contrast with humid, summery Rio: dry air, desert landscapes and preparation for the Bolivian highlands. The Events and Festivals label does not imply a festival in Atacama; the listed programmes feature sightseeing and nature here.

### Peru: Titicaca, Cusco and Machu Picchu

The Peruvian stage follows Bolivia's high-altitude lagoons, Uyuni Salt Flat and La Paz. In Peru, the itinerary includes the Puno area and Uros islands, followed by Cusco and [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/). Andean culture and ancient monuments are the focus. Machu Picchu requires precise timing and admission arrangements, but these itineraries do not promise attendance at a Peruvian festival.

## Calendar, connections and physical demands

For **Carnival versions**, choose the specific parade first and fit the flights and remaining stages around it. The Champions' Parade and the main competitive samba-school parades are different evenings. Check admission for the correct night, seating category and transfers against the chosen tour's inclusions. The word “Carnival” in the title is not enough.

For **the New Year itinerary**, December 31 in Rio is the fixed point. Allow a buffer when arranging the international arrival flight; the days after the celebration follow the established sequence. Moving this trip to a different week would undermine its main purpose.

Physical demands change too: sightseeing in large cities gives way to the Andes, long drives across Bolivia and visits to archaeological sites in Peru. Health, acclimatisation and clothing for conditions ranging from the ocean coast to cold high-altitude mornings all matter. Ada Tours helps coordinate flights, accommodation and practical preparation for the chosen itinerary, while exact services remain subject to that tour's terms.

If history and nature matter more than a particular celebration date, compare [tours in Peru](/peru/tour/) and [journeys through Chile](/chile/tour/) separately. For an event-focused trip, choose the celebration first, then the length of the journey.

## Frequently asked questions about festive tours through Argentina, Chile and Peru

### Does Carnival take place in one of the three selected countries?

No. On the qualifying tours combining these countries with the event theme, Carnival takes place in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Argentina, Chile and Peru are later stages of the longer journey.

### How does the New Year itinerary differ from Carnival?

The central event on the [New Year tour](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-5-countries-new-year-group-tour-19-days/) is New Year's Eve on Copacabana. Carnival options are tied to samba-school performances on different dates. Their geography is similar, but their calendar goals differ.

### Can the journey be shortened to Argentina, Chile and Peru?

A private itinerary covering those countries can be discussed, but the listed ready-made festival tours also include Brazil and Bolivia. Removing the Brazil stage would mean losing the very event the themed selection is built around.

### What is harder after Carnival: borders or altitude?

Both need preparation. The route crosses five countries and includes a high-altitude section from Atacama through Bolivia to Peru. Entry rules depend on nationality, while altitude requires attention to personal wellbeing and the pace of the itinerary.

This combination offers two different ways to discover local traditions. In [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), Argentine cuisine features during an evening of tango with dinner. In [Chile](/chile/), you can add a visit to wineries in the [Maipo Valley](/chile/place/maipo-valley/) and a tasting. The existing itinerary in [Peru](/peru/) is mainly devoted to archaeology and Andean cities: specialist food workshops and tastings are not separately advertised there.

The relevant itinerary is [Six Latin American Countries in 20 Days: from Rio to Machu Picchu](/multi-country/tour/latin-america-6-countries-20-days/). It also visits Brazil, Uruguay and Bolivia. Thus, the [Argentina + Chile + Peru selection](/multi-country/argentina_chile_peru/) represents the geographical intersection of a longer journey, not a separate ready-made tour limited to these three countries.

## Buenos Aires: dinner as part of a cultural evening

On the Argentina day, a tango show with dinner follows the city sightseeing tour. The programme mentions traditional dishes and Argentine wines. This is the clearest food-focused event within the three selected countries. It is part of an evening performance and should not automatically be equated with a separate sommelier-led wine tasting or winery visit.

During the day, the route explores [San Telmo](/argentina/place/san-telmo/), La Boca, Plaza de Mayo and Recoleta. This lets travellers discover the city's neighbourhoods before moving from architecture and history to a living musical tradition in the evening. If you want to study Argentine wines in depth, one dinner will not be enough: additional tastings would require an itinerary change.

## Chile: Maipo wineries need their own time slot

In [Santiago de Chile](/chile/place/santiago-de-chile/), the included sightseeing covers the historic centre, La Moneda, Plaza de Armas and Santa Lucía Hill. **The Maipo Valley winery visit with a tasting is listed separately and costs extra.** This option has a minimum of 2 participants and is not included in the base tour price.

The following day involves a flight to Calama and travel to San Pedro de Atacama before the high-altitude section through Bolivia. The winery decision is therefore best made before fixing the Santiago schedule. Winery visits and city sightseeing may require different time slots, and it would be wrong to promise that both can always fit into the day.

If tastings are the main reason for travelling, compare [food-and-wine itineraries featuring Chile](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/chile/) and arrange dedicated time for Maipo.

## Peru: what is included in the confirmed programme?

The Peru section begins at Titicaca, continues to [Cusco](/peru/place/cusco/), a visit to [Machu Picchu](/peru/place/machu-picchu/) and sightseeing in [Lima](/peru/place/lima/). This full itinerary includes high-altitude roads, visits to Inca monuments and onward transfers. Lunch is provided on one of the travel days, but the published tour does not specify a separate gastronomy excursion in Peru.

Travellers interested in local food can discuss additional restaurant time in Cusco or Lima. This must fit around excursions and flights. Cooking classes, chef-led market visits or pisco tastings should not be promised as already-included services.

Food and wine experiences are unevenly distributed here. Argentina provides an included evening with dinner; Chile an optional paid wine excursion; Peru an experience that could be added by individual agreement. Other countries and a long high-altitude section lie between them. Those stages cannot simply be deleted from the 20-day tour while retaining its duration and price.

### Is the Maipo tasting already included?

No. The Maipo Valley winery visit is an optional, paid excursion with a minimum number of participants. The included Santiago activity is a city sightseeing tour.

### Is there a gastronomy programme in Peru?

On the published itinerary, Peru's days are dedicated to Titicaca, Cusco, Machu Picchu and Lima. No separate cooking workshops or tastings are confirmed as included, though they can be discussed as itinerary changes.

### Can I visit only Argentina, Chile and Peru?

Such an option can be requested, but the ready-made tour shown here covers six countries over 20 days. A three-country journey would require new arrangements for flights, duration, activities and price.
